title: SolarWinds Orion supply-chain compromise
summary: CISA reported active exploitation involving affected SolarWinds Orion software versions.
uncertaintyNotes: Exact occurrence date, complete victim list and attack-technique links are outside this seed's verified scope.

title: Shai-Hulud npm ecosystem compromise
summary: CISA issued an alert describing a self-replicating npm ecosystem supply-chain compromise and attempted credential theft.
uncertaintyNotes: Affected individual packages and versions require package-level primary evidence before asserting links.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: Codecov Bash Uploader compromise
summary: Codecov reported that a credential exposed by an error in its Docker image creation process let an actor modify its Bash Uploader script, which could then export information from customers' CI environments. Codecov says it learned of the change on 1 April 2021.
uncertaintyNotes: Which customers' secrets were actually used is not established.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: tj-actions/changed-files GitHub Action compromise
summary: The GitHub advisory reports that attackers retroactively pointed multiple tj-actions/changed-files version tags at a malicious commit whose script extracted secrets from runner memory and printed them into GitHub Actions logs.
uncertaintyNotes: Reported usage of the Action (about 23,000 repositories) is not a count of confirmed leaks.
How the maintainer's token was obtained is reported elsewhere but not confirmed in this record.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: s1ngularity: malicious Nx npm packages
summary: Wiz reported that malicious Nx versions published to npm on 26 August 2025 ran a post-install script that harvested GitHub and npm tokens, SSH keys and other secrets, prompting installed AI CLI tools with permission-skipping flags to search the filesystem. Wiz observed over a thousand valid GitHub tokens among the leaked data.
uncertaintyNotes: The Nx maintainers' own advisory is not yet captured as a source.
How the npm publishing token was first stolen is reported by secondary sources only.
Any relationship to the Shai-Hulud npm compromise is by ecosystem only and has not been reviewed.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: CircleCI breach via malware on an engineer's laptop
summary: CircleCI reported that malware on an engineer's laptop was used to steal a valid, 2FA-backed SSO session, and recommended that all customers rotate secrets stored in the platform. CircleCI first alerted customers on 4 January 2023 and published its incident report on 12 January.
uncertaintyNotes: Impact on individual customers is not covered by this record.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: Cloudflare intrusion using credentials missed in rotation
summary: Cloudflare reported that it did not rotate one service token and three service accounts leaked in the October 2023 Okta compromise because it mistakenly believed they were unused. A threat actor used them between 14 and 17 November 2023 to access Cloudflare's Confluence wiki and Jira.
uncertaintyNotes: Attribution is Cloudflare's own assessment; no actor is recorded here.
The link to the Okta support-system breach has not been reviewed as a relationship.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: Uber S3 breach via an AWS key in a private GitHub repository
summary: The FTC states that between 13 October and 15 November 2016 intruders accessed Uber's Amazon S3 datastore using an AWS access key posted in a private GitHub repository. The intruders reached the repository with passwords exposed in other breaches, and Uber did not require multi-factor authentication for GitHub. Uber disclosed the breach on 21 November 2017.
uncertaintyNotes: Hard-coded credentials (CWE-798) is a weakness candidate only.
The captured FTC document does not show its own publication date.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: Storm-0558 use of an acquired Microsoft signing key
summary: Microsoft reported that Storm-0558 used an acquired Microsoft account (MSA) consumer signing key to forge tokens and access Outlook Web Access and Outlook.com.
uncertaintyNotes: How the key left the signing environment is unknown. Microsoft's crash-dump explanation is its leading hypothesis, and its 12 March 2024 update says no crash dump containing the key material was found.
Microsoft's earlier disclosures about Storm-0558 are not captured in this record.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: Python admin GitHub token leaked in a Docker Hub image
summary: PyPI reported that a GitHub personal access token with admin access to the python, pypi, psf and pypa organizations was found in a compiled .pyc file inside a public Docker Hub image. The token was revoked immediately and no indicators of malicious activity were found.
uncertaintyNotes: This is a researcher-found exposure with no reported attacker activity. It is typed as a breach because the feed has no exposure type.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: Microsoft AI research SAS token exposed 38TB
summary: Wiz Research reported that a Microsoft AI research GitHub repository shared files through an Azure SAS token scoped to the entire storage account, exposing 38TB of additional private data, including two employees' workstation backups. Wiz's timeline says Microsoft invalidated the token on 24 June 2023.
uncertaintyNotes: This is a researcher-found exposure with no reported attacker activity. It is typed as a breach because the feed has no exposure type.
Microsoft's own MSRC post is not yet captured as a source.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: Cloud extortion campaign using exposed .env files
summary: Unit 42 reported an extortion campaign in which attackers took AWS IAM access keys from publicly exposed .env files on web applications. The campaign targeted 110,000 domains and yielded over 90,000 unique variables.
uncertaintyNotes: This is a campaign across many organizations. It is typed as an intrusion because the feed's only campaign type is for malware campaigns.
The actor and the number of extorted organizations are not stated.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: Okta support system breach exposing session tokens in HAR files
summary: Okta reported that an actor used a service account stored in its customer support system to view files uploaded by 134 customers between 28 September and 17 October 2023. Some were HAR files containing session tokens, which the actor used to hijack the Okta sessions of 5 customers. The service account's username and password had been saved to an employee's personal Google account.
uncertaintyNotes: Okta says the credential was most likely exposed through the employee's personal Google account or personal device; the exact path is not confirmed.
Downstream incidents at Okta customers, such as Cloudflare's, are separate records; the relationship has not been reviewed.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: Toyota T-Connect access key exposed on public GitHub
summary: Toyota reported that a T-Connect website development contractor uploaded part of the site's source code, including a data server access key, to a public GitHub repository in December 2017. The code stayed public until 15 September 2022 and the key was changed on 17 September 2022. Up to 296,019 customer email addresses and customer management numbers may have been exposed.
uncertaintyNotes: Toyota says third-party access could not be confirmed from access history but could not be ruled out; no misuse had been confirmed. It is typed as a breach because the feed has no exposure type.
Toyota's notice is in Japanese; this summary is a translated paraphrase.
Hard-coded credentials (CWE-798) is a weakness candidate only.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: Uber intrusion via a compromised contractor account and MFA push approval
summary: Uber reported that an attacker compromised an external contractor's account, likely using a corporate password bought on the dark web after malware infected the contractor's personal device. The attacker repeatedly triggered two-factor login approval requests until the contractor accepted one, then reached other employee accounts with elevated permissions to tools including G-Suite and Slack, and downloaded some internal Slack messages and invoice-tool information. Uber says it did not see access to production systems, user accounts or sensitive user databases.
uncertaintyNotes: Uber attributes the attack to Lapsus$; as with other vendor attributions in this feed, no actor is recorded.

Reports that the attacker found a PowerShell script with hard-coded admin credentials for Uber's PAM system come from the attacker's own statements and secondary coverage. Uber's statement does not mention it, so it is not part of this record.
Distinct from incident:uber-github-aws-key-2016 (different year and method).
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: AI-driven intrusion campaign using a forked Cairn pentest framework
summary: Unit 42 reported that between August and September 2026 an actor it tracks as CL-STA-1238 used a customized fork of the open-source Cairn AI penetration-testing framework, running on Zhipu GLM and DeepSeek models, to conduct 25 operations against at least 19 organizations in the semiconductor, defense and civil-society sectors. Unit 42 confirmed unauthorized access or data retrieval at 10 of them; reported impacts include a persistent production API token at a semiconductor company.
uncertaintyNotes: Unit 42 assesses with moderate confidence that this is China-nexus intelligence collection; that is a hypothesis, and no actor is recorded here.
Victim organizations are unnamed; do not attribute this campaign to any specific company or customer.
This is a campaign across many organizations, typed as an intrusion because the feed's only campaign type is for malware campaigns.
Recent report (published 12 November 2026); no corrections had appeared as of 17 November 2026.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: West Pharmaceutical Services intrusion with data theft and encrypted systems
summary: West Pharmaceutical Services reported in an SEC Form 8-K that an intrusion detected on 4 May 2026 involved the exfiltration of certain data by an unauthorized party and the encryption of certain systems, temporarily disrupting its business operations globally.
uncertaintyNotes: No threat actor or ransomware group is named in the filing.
Material financial impact had not been determined at filing, and the extent of the data affected was still under investigation.
The 8-K gives 7 May 2026 as its report date and was filed on 11 May 2026; the feed uses the filing date.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: Binance internal wallet-signing service compromise
summary: Binance's preliminary report says that on 30 October 2026 (UTC+8) attackers used unauthorized access to its internal wallet signing service to start transactions outside the normal withdrawal process. As summarized by The Hacker News, the report traces the campaign to a tampered Homebrew installer an engineer downloaded in June, a fake job interview in September, and a container deployment permission token found on an engineer's computer and used on 29 October.
uncertaintyNotes: Binance's report is preliminary; it says findings will undergo further independent review. Watch for the final report.
The Binance Square report was checked through a search index on 2026-11-17 because direct fetches are blocked; the attack-chain details come from The Hacker News's summary of that report.
Amounts differ across reports (about $6.34B and $6.43B); no figure is recorded here.
No attacker is recorded: the report as summarized does not attribute this theft to a named actor.
Binance dates the incident 30 October (UTC+8); press timelines give 29 October. occurredOn is left empty until the final report.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: Novo Nordisk unauthorized access and data copied externally
summary: Novo Nordisk said on 11 June 2026 that it had identified unauthorized access to a limited number of internal IT systems and that certain non-public data, including personal data, was copied externally without authorization. It said it was investigating with external cybersecurity experts, was in contact with the relevant authorities and was informing impacted parties.
uncertaintyNotes: Later company updates, quoted in press, describe pseudonymized clinical-trial data and core operations not being affected; that update page was not captured, so those details are not in the summary.
An extortion group's claims (about 1.3 TB stolen, a $25M demand) are unconfirmed; no actor is recorded.
How the attackers got in has not been disclosed.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: Salesloft Drift OAuth tokens used to steal Salesforce data
summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group reported that from as early as 8 August through at least 18 August 2025, the actor it tracks as UNC6395 used compromised OAuth tokens for the Salesloft Drift app to export large volumes of data from many Salesforce instances, then searched the data for secrets such as AWS access keys and Snowflake tokens. Salesloft and Salesforce revoked all Drift access and refresh tokens on 20 August. Google later confirmed Drift Email tokens were used on 9 August to read mail in a very small number of Google Workspace accounts.
uncertaintyNotes: How the Drift OAuth tokens were first obtained is not covered by this source.
Counts of affected organizations vary by outlet and are not recorded here.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: Mercedes-Benz GitHub Enterprise token exposed in a public repository
summary: RedHunt Labs reported finding a GitHub token, leaked by a Mercedes-Benz employee in a personal public repository, that it says gave unrestricted access to source code on the company's internal GitHub Enterprise Server. RedHunt dates the leak to 29 September 2023, found it on 11 January 2024, and says Mercedes confirmed the leak and revoked the token on 24 January 2024.
uncertaintyNotes: Typed as breach to match the Toyota T-Connect precedent; this was an exposure with no confirmed misuse.
Mercedes said in press statements that the token reached a limited number of repositories, not the entire source code; that statement is not in this source.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: GlassWorm self-propagating VS Code extension worm
summary: Koi Security reported that seven OpenVSX extensions were compromised on 17 October 2025 with about 35,800 total downloads, and on 19 October found an infected extension in Microsoft's VS Code marketplace. The worm hid code with invisible Unicode characters, harvested npm, GitHub, OpenVSX and Git credentials, and used them to compromise more packages and extensions.
uncertaintyNotes: Later waves (November 2025 onward) are not covered by this record.
Extension counts differ between Koi's post and later reporting; Koi's figures are used here.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: Malicious LiteLLM releases on PyPI after a compromised Trivy scan
summary: LiteLLM reported that malicious versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 were live on PyPI on 24 March 2026 from 10:39 UTC for about 40 minutes before PyPI quarantined them. It believes the compromise came from the Trivy dependency in its CI/CD security scanning workflow, and that the versions carried a credential stealer that looked for environment variables, SSH keys, cloud credentials, Kubernetes tokens and database passwords.
uncertaintyNotes: The upstream Trivy compromise is not recorded as its own incident yet.
Attribution to a named actor is from third-party research and is not recorded here.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: Railway breach exposing customer environment variables
summary: Railway reported that an attacker exploited its build infrastructure on 20 October 2026, moved laterally, and decrypted a subset of customer environment variables for at most 1.85% of workspaces, about 100,000. Decrypted data included linked-account tokens, such as GitHub OAuth tokens and bring-your-own AI keys, for 1,852 users. Railway asked major providers to revoke potentially exposed keys on 21 October and estimated unauthorized spend on stolen keys at about $740,000.
uncertaintyNotes: The 1.85% figure is Railway's stated upper bound, not a confirmed count of stolen variables.
Railway has not established whether the attacker operated the services that later used the stolen keys.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: Fireworks AI incident exposing secrets in customer evaluation jobs
summary: Fireworks AI reported that on 6 October 2026 it identified unauthorized use of internal Fireworks credentials, through which a third party accessed environment variables used in evaluation jobs in a limited number of customer accounts, capturing API keys and tokens stored as secrets. It revoked the internal credentials and affected keys and rotated employee API keys and service-account tokens. A 17 November update describes this as the first of two incidents.
uncertaintyNotes: How the internal credentials were obtained has not been disclosed.
The second incident (23 to 30 October 2026) is not recorded separately yet.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.

title: Chainalysis intrusion exposing live tokens and password hashes
summary: Chainalysis reported on 30 October 2026 that an external actor using offensive agentic techniques gained unauthorized access to its systems and internal tools. A later update said names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all Chainalysis users were exposed, and that KYT, address screening and the login page were taken offline. Every user must reset passwords and rotate API keys.
uncertaintyNotes: Correction in the source: the 30 October update said there was no evidence of access to authentication credentials or session tokens; a later update on the same page reported live tokens for all users exposed.
'Offensive agentic techniques' is the company's wording; the tooling used is not recorded.
No ATT&CK technique is asserted until a separate sourced mapping review.
